title: Plant Parts and Functions
seo_title: Primary 4 Science: Plant Parts and Functions Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 4: Plant system (Plant parts and functions)
standard_text: Identify the parts of a plant (leaf, stem and root) and their functions: leaves make food, the stem holds the plant up and carries water and food, and roots hold the plant in the soil and take in water and mineral salts. Recognise that the plant parts work together as a system (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on plant parts and their functions: leaves, stem, roots, flowers, plant parts we eat, and experiments. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Leaves make food; roots take in water.
key_sub: The stem holds the plant up and carries water and food.
body_html:
How to think about it

Each part of a plant has a job, and the parts work together as a system.

  • Leaves make food using light.
  • Stem holds the plant up and carries water (from the roots) and food (from the leaves).
  • Roots hold the plant in the soil and take in water and mineral salts.
  • Flowers develop into fruits with seeds.

Some parts also store food: sweet potato (root), ginger and sugar cane (stem).

Example

All the leaves of a plant are removed. What happens?

Leaves make food

No leaves, no food

Answer: The plant grows weakly or dies.

Example

A celery stalk stands in red water. Where does the red colour go?

Water is taken in at the bottom

It moves up through the stem

Answer: Up the stem to the leaves.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking roots take in food from the soil. Plants make their own food in the leaves.
  • Thinking ginger and potatoes are roots. They are underground stems.
  • Forgetting that the stem carries food down as well as water up.
  • Changing more than one thing in a plant experiment.

faq.q: What are the functions of the roots?
faq.a: Roots hold the plant firmly in the soil and take in water and mineral salts.
The stem holds the plant upright and carries water from the roots to the leaves and food from the leaves to other parts.
No. Ginger is an underground stem. It has buds that can grow into new shoots, and it stores food.

items.q: Which part of a plant helps to carry food from the leaves to other parts?
items.e: The stem helps to carry food from the leaves to other parts.

items.q: Which part of a plant does this job: it makes seeds so that new plants can grow?
items.e: Each part has its own job.

items.q: Which part of a plant holds it firmly in the soil?
items.e: Roots spread into the soil and anchor the plant.

items.q: Which part of a plant helps to make fruits and seeds?
items.e: The flowers help to make fruits and seeds.

items.q: Which part of a plant helps to carry water from the roots to the leaves?
items.e: The stem helps to carry water from the roots to the leaves.

items.q: Look at the plant. Which letter points to the roots?
items.e: The flower is at the top, the leaves come off the stem, and the roots are under the soil.

items.q: Which part of a plant makes food?
items.e: Leaves use light to make food.

items.q: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
items.e: Roots take in water and mineral salts.

items.q: Look at the plant. Which part is labelled C?
items.e: The flower is at the top, the leaves come off the stem, and the roots are under the soil.

items.q: Which part of a plant carries food from the leaves to other parts?
items.e: Food made in the leaves is carried by the stem to the roots, fruits and seeds.

items.q: Which part of a plant helps to take in water and mineral salts from the soil?
items.e: The roots help to take in water and mineral salts from the soil.

items.q: Look at the plant. Which letter points to the flower?
items.e: The flower is at the top, the leaves come off the stem, and the roots are under the soil.

items.q: What does the stem do?
c: It takes in water from the soil.
It holds the plant up and carries water and food.
items.e: The stem connects the roots to the leaves.

items.q: What do the flowers of a plant develop into?
items.e: Seeds grow into new plants.

items.q: What is the job of the flower of a plant?
c: to hold the plant up and carry water from the roots to the leaves
to use sunlight to make food for the plant
to make seeds so that new plants can grow
to take in water and nutrients from the soil and hold the plant firmly in the ground
items.e: Roots drink, stems hold up, leaves make food, flowers make seeds.

items.q: Look at the plant. Which part is labelled B?
items.e: The flower is at the top, the leaves come off the stem, and the roots are under the soil.

items.q: What is the job of the roots of a plant?
c: to hold the plant up and carry water from the roots to the leaves
to make seeds so that new plants can grow
to use sunlight to make food for the plant
to take in water and nutrients from the soil and hold the plant firmly in the ground
items.e: Roots drink, stems hold up, leaves make food, flowers make seeds.

items.q: Look at the plant. Which letter points to the roots?
items.e: The flower is at the top, the leaves come off the stem, and the roots are under the soil.

items.q: Which two parts of a plant are usually above the ground?
items.e: The roots are usually under the soil.

items.q: Does a plant take in food from the soil?
c: No. It takes in water and mineral salts; it makes its own food in the leaves.
items.e: Soil does not give plants food.

items.q: A sweet potato is a swollen root. What is stored in it?
items.e: Food is carried down the stem and stored in the root.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Which does the water pass through first: the stem or the leaves and flowers?
c: Water does not pass through either.
They happen at the same time.
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.

items.q: Which part of a plant helps to hold the plant upright?
items.e: The stem helps to hold the plant upright.

items.q: Why is sugar cane sweet?
c: Its stem stores the sugar made in the leaves.
It takes in sugar from the soil.
items.e: The stem stores food.

items.q: A healthy plant was left for two weeks after its roots were cut off. What most likely happened?
c: It cannot take in water and mineral salts, so it wilts and dies.
items.e: Each part of the plant has a job; the plant needs all of them.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Where does it go after the roots?
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.

items.q: A healthy plant was left for two weeks after it was kept in a dark cupboard. What most likely happened?
c: Its leaves cannot make food, so it grows weakly.
items.e: Each part of the plant has a job; the plant needs all of them.

items.q: Why do some plants grow tall stems?
c: to reach more light for their leaves
items.e: Taller plants are not shaded by others.

items.q: How do the roots and the leaves work together?
c: Roots take in water for the leaves to use in making food, and leaves make food for the roots.
Leaves take in water for the roots.
Roots make food for the leaves.
They do not need each other.
items.e: Parts of a plant work as a system.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Which does the water pass through first: the stem or the roots?
c: They happen at the same time.
Water does not pass through either.
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.

items.q: A healthy plant was left for two weeks after its stem was bent and broken. What most likely happened?
c: Water cannot reach the leaves, so the leaves wilt.
items.e: Each part of the plant has a job; the plant needs all of them.

items.q: Which part of a plant helps to hold the plant firmly in the soil?
items.e: The roots help to hold the plant firmly in the soil.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Where does it go after the leaves and flowers?
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.

items.q: Which plant part would be damaged by a caterpillar that eats leaves?
c: the part that holds the plant in the soil
the part that takes in water
items.e: Leaves make food.

items.q: A plant has many fine, hair-like roots. How does this help?
c: They give a large surface to take in more water.
items.e: More roots touch more soil water.

items.q: Which part of a plant is like a 'pipe' that carries water?
items.e: Tubes in the stem carry water up.

items.q: A tree is a plant. Which plant part is the trunk of a tree?
items.e: Trees have the same parts as other flowering plants: a trunk is a big, woody stem.

items.q: A tree is a plant. Which plant part is the roots under the ground of a tree?
items.e: Trees have the same parts as other flowering plants: a trunk is a big, woody stem.

items.q: A healthy plant was left for two weeks after all its leaves were removed. What most likely happened?
c: It cannot make enough food, so it grows weakly or dies.
items.e: Each part of the plant has a job; the plant needs all of them.

items.q: Why do the leaves of a plant wilt when the roots are damaged?
c: The leaves make too much food.
Not enough water can be taken in and carried to the leaves.
The flowers take all the water.
items.e: The plant parts work together.

sets.title: Plant parts we eat and use

items.q: Why do the leaves of most plants face the light?
c: to get more light to make food
items.e: Leaves need light to make food.

items.q: Why does a gardener tie a young papaya plant to a stick?
c: to help it take in water
Its stem is not yet strong enough to hold it up.
items.e: The stick helps support the plant.

items.q: A plant is kept in a dark cupboard, so its leaves get no light. What will most likely happen to the plant?
c: Water cannot reach the leaves, so they dry up.
It cannot make seeds for new plants.
It cannot take in water, so it wilts.
It cannot make its food, so it grows weakly.
items.e: Each part does a job the plant needs.

items.q: Why is ginger called an underground stem and not a root?
c: It has buds that grow into new shoots.
items.e: Roots do not have buds.

items.q: Why should we not pull up a plant when moving it to a new pot?
c: The flowers will turn into seeds.
The leaves will fall off at once.
The roots may be damaged and the plant cannot take in water.
items.e: Keep the roots and soil together.

items.q: Which part of the plant do we eat when we eat tapioca?
items.e: We eat the root of the tapioca plant.

items.q: A plant has been watered but its leaves are still drooping on a hot day. What is the most likely reason?
c: It is making too much food.
It is losing water from its leaves faster than its roots can take it in.
items.e: Plants lose water through their leaves on hot days.

items.q: Which part of the plant do we eat when we eat spinach?
items.e: We eat the leaves of the spinach plant.

items.q: Which part of the plant do we eat when we eat ginger?
items.e: Ginger grows underground, but it is a stem: it has buds and grows sideways.

items.q: Which part of a pandan plant do we use in cooking?
items.e: Pandan leaves give a sweet smell to kueh and rice.

items.q: Which part of the plant do we eat when we eat chilli?
items.e: We eat the fruit of the chilli plant.

items.q: Which part of the plant do we eat when we eat lady's fingers (okra)?
items.e: We eat the fruit of the lady's fingers plant.

items.q: Which part of the plant do we eat when we eat peanuts?
items.e: We eat the seeds of the peanuts plant.

items.q: A tree's trunk is badly damaged all the way round. What will most likely happen to the plant?
c: It cannot make its food, so it grows weakly.
It cannot take in water, so it wilts.
It cannot make seeds for new plants.
Water cannot reach the leaves, so they dry up.
items.e: Each part does a job the plant needs.

items.q: Why does a money plant have roots along its stem?
c: to cling to a wall or a pole so it can climb towards light
items.e: These roots help the weak stem to climb.

items.q: Which part of the plant do we eat when we eat sweet potato?
items.e: We eat the root of the sweet potato plant.

items.q: Why are some stems, such as the stem of the kangkong, hollow and soft?
c: They do not need to hold up a heavy plant and help it float in water.
They make food in the roots.
items.e: Kangkong grows in water and wet soil.

items.q: Why does a cactus have a thick, green stem?
c: to store water and make food
items.e: Its leaves are spines, so the green stem makes food.

items.q: Which part of the plant do we eat when we eat mango?
items.e: We eat the fruit of the mango plant.

items.q: Which of these vegetables is a leaf?
items.e: We eat the leaves and soft stems of kangkong.

items.q: A healthy plant was left for two weeks after all its flowers were picked off. What most likely happened?
c: It cannot make fruits and seeds.
items.e: Each part of the plant has a job; the plant needs all of them.

items.q: Which part of a plant carries water up to the leaves?
items.e: It has tiny tubes inside.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Which does the water pass through first: the soil or the leaves and flowers?
c: Water does not pass through either.
They happen at the same time.
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.

items.q: What are root hairs for?
c: taking in water from the soil
items.e: Tiny hairs on the roots.

items.q: Why is food colouring used in the celery investigation?
c: so we can see where the water goes
items.e: Water is clear.

items.q: Where does water go after it reaches the leaves?
c: It goes back down to the roots.
It stays in the leaf for ever.
Most of it evaporates into the air.
items.e: Through tiny holes.

items.q: Why do some plants such as the rain tree have a thick, woody trunk?
c: to hold up the heavy branches and leaves
to take in water from the air
items.e: A strong stem holds the plant up.

items.q: Which part of a plant takes in water?
items.e: From the soil.

items.q: Which way does water travel in a plant?
c: down, from the leaves to the roots
up, from the roots to the leaves
items.e: Roots are at the bottom.

items.q: A tree is very tall. How does water reach the top leaves?
c: It does not reach the top.
Rain falls straight into the top leaves only.
It travels up tiny tubes in the trunk.
items.e: A trunk is a stem.

items.q: What does a white flower in red water look like after a day?
items.e: The water reaches the petals.

items.q: Why does a plant in a sunny window need watering more often than one in a shady corner?
c: More water evaporates from its leaves.
items.e: Warm and sunny: more evaporation.

items.q: Aisha stood a white daisy in a jar of water with blue food colouring. Where will the blue colour appear after a day?
c: only at the bottom of the stem
nowhere, the colour stays in the jar
items.e: The coloured water travels up the stem to the top of the plant.

items.q: What happens to a plant that does not get enough water?
items.e: Water keeps it firm.

items.q: A pot plant's leaves droop on a hot day. What will help it most?
items.e: Roots take up the water.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Which does the water pass through first: the air or the soil?
c: Water does not pass through either.
They happen at the same time.
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.

items.q: Farah stood a Chinese cabbage leaf in a jar of water with blue food colouring. Why does the colour spread up the plant?
c: The plant takes up the coloured water through tiny tubes in its stem.
The colour floats up through the air.
items.e: The tubes carry water up from the bottom.

items.q: Ethan stood a white rose in a jar of water with blue food colouring. Why does the colour spread up the plant?
c: The colour floats up through the air.
The plant takes up the coloured water through tiny tubes in its stem.
items.e: The tubes carry water up from the bottom.

items.q: Rachel stood a white rose in a jar of water with green food colouring. When the stem is cut across, what will Rachel see?
c: a green stem all the way through, like paint
small green dots, which are the ends of the water tubes
items.e: The tubes carry the water up the stem.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Which does the water pass through first: the stem or the soil?
c: Water does not pass through either.
They happen at the same time.
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.

items.q: A plant's roots are left in dry soil for weeks. What will most likely happen to the plant?
c: It cannot make seeds for new plants.
It cannot take in water, so it wilts.
It cannot make its food, so it grows weakly.
Water cannot reach the leaves, so they dry up.
items.e: Each part does a job the plant needs.

items.q: A pupil put a plant with roots in a measuring cylinder of water and covered the water with oil. The water level dropped. Why?
c: The water evaporated through the oil.
items.e: The oil stops evaporation, so the water went into the plant.

items.q: Siti placed a white flower in water with blue colouring. After a day, the petals turned blue. What does this show?
c: The colouring is food for the flower.
Water travels down from the flower.
Water travels up the stem to the flower.
items.e: The coloured water was carried up through the stem.

items.q: A pupil grew two identical plants. Plant P had all its leaves; plant Q had half its leaves removed. Which plant grew taller after 3 weeks?
items.e: More leaves make more food for growth.

items.q: Imran stood a white daisy in a jar of water with blue food colouring. What does this investigation show?
c: Water travels up the stem to the leaves and flowers.
Water travels down from the leaves to the roots.
Leaves take in water from the air.
items.e: The colour is a way of seeing where the water goes.

items.q: Nurul stood a stick of celery with its leaves in a jar of water with blue food colouring. When the stem is cut across, what will Nurul see?
c: a blue stem all the way through, like paint
small blue dots, which are the ends of the water tubes
items.e: The tubes carry the water up the stem.

items.e: The tubes carried the red water up.

so that only one variable is changed
items.e: This makes the test fair.
